Profile Vildagliptin is an inhibitor of the enzyme dipeptidylpeptidase-4, an enzyme responsible, among other roles, for the degradation of the incretin hormone glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1; insulino- tropin), which plays a role in regulating insulin secretion. Vilda- gliptin is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (p.431); it may be added to metformin, a sulfonylurea, or a thiazolidine- dione, when monotherapy with these is insufficient. It is given orally in a dose of 50 mg twice daily when given with metformin or a thiazolidinedione, and in a dose of 50 mg once daily in the morning when given with a sulfonylurea. A total daily dose of more than 100 mg of vildagliptin is not recommended, and in patients taking a combination of vildagliptin with a sulfonylurea, a dose of vildagliptin 100 mg daily is no more effective than vil- dagliptin 50 mg daily.
